senses: A tropical Asian grass, Cymbopogon nardus, that has citrus-scented leaves.
An essential oil obtained from this plant, often used as an insect repellent.
Mysterious and often incomprehensible yet seemingly wise.
ety: From French gnomique, ultimately from Ancient Greek γνωμικός (gnōmikós), from γνώμη (gnṓmē, “thought, judgement”), akin to γιγνώσκω (gignṓskō, “know”). By surface analysis, gnome + -ic.
examples: He always makes gnomic utterances.
The gnomic belief that the world is conditioned by love is no idle apothegm.
In his part gnomic, part mechanic’s style, Mr. Pirsig’s narrator declares that the real world is a seamless continuum of the material and metaphysical.

senses: A person who is selected.
A specific breed of small, red pepper originally from Peru
examples: Piquillos are not edible raw; instead, they're smoke-roasted, then packed in jars.

senses: One who gips (cleans fish in preparation for curing).
ety: From gip (“clean [fish] for curing”) + -er (agent noun suffix).

senses: Someone or something that scrambles (in various senses).
A vine that does not attach itself to its supports.
A device that makes messages intentionally, but reversibly, unintelligible for reasons of privacy or security.
A motorcycle used for motocross.
examples: May it comfort us latter-day scramblers up that fine old mountain to know that Le Conte found it "difficult and fatiguing in the extreme."
In the movies spies are always talking over cell phones with built-in scramblers.

senses: A person who or thing that slits.
Shears for slitting sheet metal.
One thousand volts. Symbol: kV or KV.
Study of the processes devised and adopted for the punishment and prevention of crime.
An automated phone call, commonly for telemarketing purposes, that uses both an autodialer and a recorded message.
ety: From robo- + call. First use appears c. 1998 in the Associated Press Newswire.
examples: The e-mailers are upset about “robocalls”—pre-recorded, automated phone calls containing anti-Democratic political messages.
Things are at least as bad on mobile phones, which were the lucky recipients of 48 billion robocalls in the United States alone last year.

senses: An alcoholic drink made from unfermented grape juice and cognac.
The imitation of biological designs or processes in engineering; biomimetics.
A proponent of centralism.
Thin, white noodles usually served cold with sauce for dipping.
ety: Borrowed from Japanese 素麺 (sōmen, “white noodles”).

senses: Synonym of kissaten, a type of Japanese café.
ety: Borrowed from Japanese 喫茶 (kissa, “tea house”).
examples: Jazz kissa are niche Japanese cafes stacked with whisky, vinyl and high-end audio systems.
All Blues, which opened October 2023, sticks to the quieter, more contemplative atmosphere that characterizes the traditional jazz kissa.

senses: Having a toothed margin, usually fish scales
Comb-like in shape.
In the manner of a collage, or of the making of a collage.
In the International System of Units, the derived unit of radioactive activity; the activity of a quantity of radioactive material in which one nucleus decays per second. Symbol: Bq
ety: Borrowed from French becquerel. Named after the French physicist Henri Becquerel.

senses: Something or someone that is assessed.
A poor or faulty adjustment, especially of a mechanism.
The inability to adapt oneself to the needs of others, or to the stresses of normal life.
To add caffeine to something.
The smallest division of a manor under the control of a commander of an order of knights, originally only the Knights Hospitaller.
A chapter of a secret order, especially the Knights Templar (order affiliated with Freemasonry).
ety: From French commanderie, from Late Latin commendaria, from Latin commendare. In the Chinese administrative division sense, used as a translation of 府 (fǔ) and 郡 (jùn).

senses: An instrument for sleeking or making smooth.
examples: The blackwashing is here to be the very last operation, and to be well performed, and when dry must be polished by a large sleeker fitting the circle of the cylinder.

senses: The wood of such trees
The resin of such trees.
ety: From New Latin, from Spanish guayacán.

senses: Any green vegetable.
The larger leaves and the seed capsules of Indian hemp which are used to make bhang.
ety: From Hindi सब्ज़ी (sabzī), from Classical Persian سبزی (sabzī).

senses: A dog; a pooch.
examples: A doggie diner, a poochie playdate, a puppy kindergarten. No matter, you will not be embarrassed. Surely people have always loved their dogs this much, that is what I tell myself, and you will too.

senses: Synonym of pancake.
Something that sells quickly in large volumes, in the manner of proverbial hotcakes.
examples: For breakfast he ordered a stack of hotcakes with butter and syrup.
Monsieur Kopay's account of coming-out in the locker room has returned to the printers for a third run. That little hotcake is coming out of Arbor house at a selling rate of 650 copies per day.

senses: A bonus; additional pay; money.
ety: Costermonger jargon bunts, perhaps from bonus.

senses: Miss, a young Korean, usually unmarried woman. Used as a form of address
Covered with or wearing a mitt.
Having fur on the feet that is a different colour from the rest of the coat.
examples: Use only your mitted hand to reach into the oven.

senses: The state of being a pundit.
The opinion or advice of a pundit.
The behaviour of a pundit.
A breakfast dish based on uncooked rolled oats and fruit.
ety: From Alemannic German Müesli, a diminutive of Mues (“a mashed dish”); compare Dutch moes.

senses: A small brown passerine bird, Alauda arvensis, that sings as it flies high into the air.
ety: From sky + lark. Verb sense 1809, originally nautical, possibly influenced by northern English dialectal term lake/laik (“to play”) (from Old Norse leika (“to play (as opposed to work)”)); see lark for details.

senses: Wood of a teak tree.
An item of craftsmanship made from teak.
A wooded area with many teak trees.
To speed away to another place by means of a vehicle with tires, or in simulation of it.
ety: Onomatopoeic. Lexicalized from Riverdale Shawty’s feature in the original mixtape version of Waka Flocka Flame’s 2009 song O Let's Do It uttering Even got the spots (Scurt! Scurt!) off the block. Then in late 2013 Chief Keef picked up the interjection, alleged to have circulated sporadically in Afro-American circles since the 1990s, for his piece Chiefin Keef, his line Pull off in that foreign, skrr skrr skrr, she thought she seen a beast, and many other lines in his further career, to be imitated by other rappers of New York and soon the whole world, which embraced it as a fashion symbol prin
examples: Gotta do the dash when I skrrt out the block Double-do a rack when your girl git the top

senses: A practitioner of Ayurvedic medicine.
examples: Like the sannyāsī, the religious ascetic, moreover, the vaidya did not adhere rigidly to the stringent rules of ritual purity which regulated the lives of the ordinary members of the higher classes.
If a prescribed sēva such as the feeding of Brahmans or the poor was not carried out by a patient, then the vaidya considered himself likely to be affected by the patient's karma.

senses: The political doctrine that holds that all people in a society should have equal rights from birth.
examples: The gap between rich and poor is growing in ways that mock American middle-class egalitarianism.

senses: Sentimentally affectionate.
Tending to kiss.
Tending to kiss frequently.
Suited to kissing; resembling or relating to kissing.
examples: We sat behind an obnoxiously kissy couple in the cinema.
Kissy face, kissy face / Sent to your phone, but / I'm tryna kiss your lips for real (uh-huh, uh-huh)

senses: A traitor or hypocrite, such as a co-worker or friend assumed trustworthy but who figuratively attacks when one's back is turned.
Indicating that the piece is to be played very loudly.
